steps.what: Monitor patient responses using direct observation and physiological monitoring equipment

tasks.design: Keep continuous patient observation and interpretation with the qualified practitioner. Existing physiological monitors, represented by {OTHER}, support observation; their current runtime does not constitute removable nurse labour.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readings require clinical interpretation and checking against the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing monitoring equipment assists observation without replacing vigilance.
tasks.still_hard: Artefacts and rapidly changing physiology can resemble one another.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner checks the patient and distinguishes a measurement problem from deterioration.
tasks.altitude: Monitoring responsibility and attendance time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Communicate a change in monitored response
reach.learn: Shared clinical escalation and trend interpretation

evidence.claim: Retaining continuous clinical observation is an E1 assessment from model knowledge; the digest gives no anaesthesia monitoring replacement case.

assumptions: Boundary is nurse monitoring and interpretation, excluding treatment administration and separate record production.
Existing monitors produce readings; nurse observation and verification remain fully counted. No free deterioration label or automatic clinical response is assumed.
Keep current equipment; no custom monitoring tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no process changes; confirm national professional scope locally.
unknowns: Equipment, staffing requirements and escalation protocols
research_questions: Which apparent monitor changes most often require bedside verification?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; continuous vigilance remains counted and existing device runtime earns no labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select, order and administer anaesthetic treatment

steps.what: Select anesthetics, adjuvant drugs, fluids or blood products for the patient
Verify authorisation, enter treatment orders and review medication safety alerts
Perform bedside checks and administer authorised drugs, fluids or blood products

tasks.design: Retain clinical selection, authorised ordering and bedside administration. The electronic prescribing record, represented by {OTHER}, retains existing medication safety checks; no new autonomous prescribing or dosing is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Treatment depends on physiology, contraindications and professional authority.
tasks.enabler_now: Rule-based medication checks already support prescribing but do not replace the clinical decision.
tasks.still_hard: Urgency and changing patient responses can require immediate reassessment.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner reconciles the order, actual preparation and patient at the bedside.
tasks.altitude: Treatment responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss an unresolved medication safety concern

evidence.claim: G-Standaard supports interaction, contraindication, dose and duplicate medication checks; this does not establish automatic anaesthetic prescribing.

assumptions: Boundary is nurse selection, order verification and administration; preparation is owned by the equipment and supplies task and must not count twice.

Existing authorised clinical assessment and protocols feed s1. Qualified preparation staff or the separately counted preparation task supplies prepared treatment after the order and before s3; their existing effort is unchanged.

This scenario requires the nurse to hold applicable ordering authority; where a separate prescriber is required, their decision remains outside this denominator and is not treated as free newly delegated work.
Retain native prescribing checks; zero upkeep because no workflow change is proposed. National prescribing and professional scope require confirmation.
unknowns: Practitioner authority, independent check requirements and preparation ownership
research_questions: Which orders require a separately authorised prescriber or independent bedside check?

approvals.approved_version: Exact patient, treatment, dose, route, timing and authorised order version; any change voids approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; selection, safety verification and physical administration retain all time. Existing medication rule runtime is not nurse effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Select and prepare anaesthesia equipment and supplies

steps.what: Select equipment, monitors, supplies and drugs appropriate to the anaesthetic plan
Prepare and check selected equipment, monitors, supplies and drugs for anaesthetic use

tasks.design: Retain patient-specific selection, physical preparation and function checks. Approved instructions in {DOCS} support preparation; a completed screen checklist does not prove equipment or prepared drugs are safe to use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Readiness requires physical examination, connections and verification.
tasks.enabler_now: Documentation tools do not replace hands-on preparation.
tasks.still_hard: A selected component can be defective, incompatible or incorrectly prepared.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner detects a mismatch between the plan and actual equipment or preparation.
tasks.altitude: Preparation responsibility and time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Describe a failed equipment readiness check
reach.learn: Fault communication and safe equipment isolation

evidence.claim: Retaining patient-specific anaesthesia preparation is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is selection and physical readiness preparation; actual drug administration and ongoing patient monitoring belong to their own tasks.
The authorised clinician supplies the existing anaesthetic plan and orders before preparation; no new structured ready or compatible flag is assumed.
Current equipment instructions remain; no custom tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes. Assign shared drug preparation once across task roll-up.
unknowns: Equipment and preparation procedures and responsibility split
research_questions: Which readiness failures are only found during physical checks?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; selection and preparation keep full time with no invented checklist-entry baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assess medical histories for anaesthesia response

steps.what: Assess patients' medical histories and clarify information relevant to predicted anesthesia response

tasks.design: Keep history interpretation and clarification with the practitioner, using the clinical record represented by {OTHER}. General record-question tools in the digest do not establish reliable prediction of anaesthesia response.
tasks.previous_blocker: Response assessment depends on incomplete histories and clinical context.
tasks.enabler_now: Record access assists review without validating an individual response forecast.
tasks.still_hard: Missing or inaccurate prior-event descriptions may materially change the assessment.
tasks.human_edge: The practitioner probes uncertainty and recognises when specialist review is needed.
tasks.altitude: Clinical assessment rights and time remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: Delphyr answers record questions with certification described as in progress; the digest does not establish anaesthesia-response prediction.

assumptions: Boundary is clinical history assessment, not a new record summary or separate documentation task.
Existing treating staff maintain source history and the patient supplies clarifications; no free structured anaesthesia-risk label is assumed.
Retain native record access; no custom prediction tool proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes; national professional scope needs confirmation.
unknowns: History completeness and specialist referral arrangements
research_questions: Which missing history details require clarification before an assessment can be used?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0; clinical history interpretation and clarification keep all time without assuming a separate removable summary task.

role.altitude: Keep anaesthesia vigilance, clinical selection, physical preparation and history judgement with qualified practitioners.
reach: Describe equipment faults to biomedical technicians
role.ambitious_version: A practitioner who maintains patient-specific vigilance and makes clinical uncertainty explicit before and during anaesthesia.
